sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Lake County
sections.html:
Valuing and billing are separate jobs in Painesville. The Auditor sets values for over 111,000 parcels, and the Treasurer mails bills and takes payment. Ohio law calls for a full reappraisal every six years and a value update midway, in year three. The Auditor has no power over the amount of tax, because voter-approved levies drive the rate.

Numbers worth keeping handy: the Auditor's real estate staff at (440) 350-2532 for owner address changes and credit questions, the Treasurer's billing line at (440) 350-2516 and the delinquent tax division at 440-350-2473. The Treasurer's main office keeps counter hours from 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays at 105 Main Street, and any parcel can be looked up through the Auditor's real property search.

Ohio bills real estate tax in two halves. The next two payment dates for Lake County come from the Treasurer's welcome page.

Pay after the deadline and a 10 percent penalty is added, with interest running twice a year on balances the county certifies as unpaid. A postal postmark on or before the date counts. Section 323.13 contains a rule many owners miss: the tax is owed whether or not a bill reached you. Call if nothing shows up by February 1 or July 1. Bills go out in mid-January and mid-June, with payment due roughly 20 to 30 days afterward. Manufactured homes run on their own calendar, also posted by the Treasurer.

sections.h2: How to challenge your property value
sections.html:
A Lake County owner can contest the valuation but never the rate. The filing season for a complaint on form DTE 1 runs January 1 to March 31 every year, and the next one opens January 1, 2027.

  • A three person panel hears the case: the Auditor, the Treasurer and the commissioners' president.
  • Bring proof with the complaint, or file it at least five days before your hearing date.
  • Expect roughly a quarter hour for a house, then a written decision about two to three weeks later.
  • Evidence the county names: a recent arm's length sale, a purchase agreement or listing, an appraisal dated to the January 1 lien date, damage photos, an insurance value, a broker's market analysis, or construction cost for a newer home including land.
  • Arguments the Board cannot weigh: how much your bill went up in percent, and how nearby parcels were valued.

Unhappy with the ruling? Form DTE 4 takes the case to the state Board of Tax Appeals within 30 days of the mailing date, and the county Court of Common Pleas is the other route. An appraiser whose report you submit has to show up and testify to it.

sections.h2: Tax relief after the 2025 reform bills
sections.html:
Five property tax reform bills, Ohio House Bills 186, 335, 124, 129 and 309, were signed on December 19, 2025, with adjustments phased in over three years. The first affects the July 2026 bill, where applicable credits or reductions are printed. Residential, agricultural and most business properties qualify without an application, and the Treasurer advises contacting your mortgage company once the credit shows so the escrow payment can be adjusted.

The homestead credit is doubled for 2026 tax payable in 2027, while the owner occupancy credit is not. For the details, call the Auditor's real estate desk at 440-350-2532. The homestead exemption is means tested for new participants, so ask for the current household income limit before you apply.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a house sells
sections.html:
An ordinary sale settles the current year's tax at closing, usually through a title company. The county's pro-rating page is written for sheriff sales: after a sale is confirmed, the Treasurer gives the total due at that time and prorates the following year's tax from the current year's full-year real estate tax plus long-term assessments such as lighting or storm water. The proration starts 90 days after the sheriff sale, and requests go to the Treasurer by email. The figure is an estimate, and the Treasurer is not responsible for later garbage bills, levy changes or value changes.

The deed transfer charge is a separate line at the Auditor: $4.00 per $1,000 of price plus fifty cents for each parcel. Section 319.202 assigns it to the seller. If you are enrolled in the Treasurer's automatic payment plan, know that a final bill is never drawn through that plan, so the closing agent has to pay it.

sections.h2: If your Lake County tax is behind
sections.html:
The Treasurer's pages lay out what happens as a balance ages:

  • A delinquent payment plan for primary residences and manufactured homes runs two years, with a down payment equal to half a year's tax and an appointment required.
  • A tax lien sale can include a property with delinquency in three billing cycles after multiple notices and newspaper publication. It is not a sale of the property. An administrative fee of $100.00 applies with the first notice and $200.00 on the sale date, and the sale is generally held every fall.
  • Lien sales can lead to 18 percent interest and added fees.
  • The Treasurer holds the first and best lien on real property. A lien purchaser can ask for foreclosure if the lien is not repaid or on a plan within 18 months, and the county prosecutor can also file in the Treasurer's name, which may lead to a sheriff sale.

A seller who owes back tax can still sell if the payoff clears at closing, so ask the delinquent tax division for a written payoff figure before signing a contract.

Lake County had 232,217 residents in July 2025 and 107,571 housing units. Three of every four households own (75.8 percent), a typical owned home is worth about $214,100, and owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,500.

Five townships, nine villages, nine cities, ten school districts and eight library systems share each bill, so a parcel's total rate depends on which of those districts it sits in. Ask the Auditor which districts your parcel falls into before you quote taxes to a buyer.

sections.h2: Preparing to sell with taxes in mind
sections.html: Start by looking up your parcel in the Auditor's real property search and checking that the owner name and address are right. Pull your most recent bill and find out whether both halves are paid. If you receive a credit, tell your title company, since the buyer may need to apply for it in their own name. If you plan to list soon, call the Auditor's real estate desk about any pending change in value, and ask your mortgage company whether an escrow refund will follow the sale.

faqs.q: When are Lake County real estate taxes due for 2026 tax payable in 2027?
faqs.a: The first half is due February 24, 2027 and the second half July 21, 2027, as posted on the Treasurer's page.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Lake County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Only the value is open to challenge. The rate comes from levies, and the Board does not hear complaints about taxes. Use form DTE 1 during the January 1 to March 31 season.

faqs.q: What does Lake County charge the seller to transfer the deed?
faqs.a: The Auditor charges $4.00 per $1,000 of price and $0.50 per parcel. That splits into a state piece of $1.00 and a county piece of $3.00, the latter passed by the commissioners on March 26, 1990.

faqs.q: What is the penalty on late Lake County property tax?
faqs.a: Ten percent, with twice-a-year interest on certified balances. A missing bill is no excuse under section 323.13. A payment plan can keep the debt from growing.

faqs.q: Can a Lake County homeowner who is behind on tax arrange a payment plan?
faqs.a: Yes, for a primary residence or manufactured home. The plan lasts two years, starts with an appointment and a down payment equal to half a year of tax, and is arranged at 440-350-2473.
